implementationPlan.note:
ALL FOUR PRESCRIBED FIXTURES BUILT AND EXECUTING GREEN. No production file was touched: every named guard was reachable from the outside, so the step's "touch a production file only if a seam genuinely cannot be reached" condition never fired.

To turn the arms green the step's own words required executing them, so the runner block landed here rather than in step 4. Step 4 keeps its denominator and set-equality work and re-verifies the untouched rostered assertions.

1. PLAN — reached through the PRODUCTION frame reader, not a literal. `decideIntentSurface` hands a surface body to `frameOfSurface` and requires the result to be CONNECTED with exactly one offer, so the affordance genuinely survives `offerOf` (commandId/commandKind/targetAggregateId/expectedVersion). A hand-built SurfaceFrame literal would have been this file's own idea of a valid frame and would keep passing after the reader tightened. POSITIVE CONTROL INSIDE THE ARM: the same frame first authorizes the run it was offered for and must return AUTHORIZED, throwing with code@layer otherwise. Only then is the foreign subject asked. So APPROVAL_SURFACE_UNREAD, APPROVAL_SURFACE_NOT_CONNECTED and APPROVAL_AFFORDANCE_ABSENT are all provably out of reach and APPROVAL_AFFORDANCE_SUBJECT_MISMATCH is the only verdict left.

2. BUDGET — real store, real material, real digest, then ONE hex digit moved. `oneHexOff` preserves length, case and alphabet, so the HEX64 fence cannot answer. POSITIVE CONTROL INSIDE THE ARM: the EXACT digest is verified first and must return ok:true, which proves the material was available and the recompute reached the comparison — that rules out both BUDGET_COMMITMENT_REF_MALFORMED and BUDGET_COMMITMENT_MATERIAL_UNAVAILABLE and leaves BOOTSTRAP_BUDGET_COMMITMENT_MISMATCH as the only reachable code. The two arms flip DIFFERENT positions (0 and 63) so they are not one fixture run twice.

  MEASURED CORRECTION, red-first and disclosed: my first draft used bootstrap's bare `openStore()` and the three budget arms went RED with `BUDGET_COMMITMENT_MATERIAL_UNAVAILABLE@DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` — the fixture had not seeded a world, so the guard under test was unreachable. That is exactly the failure the positive control exists to catch, and it caught it on the first run. Fixed by moving to `openHostileStore`, whose `assertActivationWorldSeeded` read-back is what makes the seeded world a measured fact rather than an assumption. ONE memoized store for all four budget legs, so the race genuinely races two callers against one commitment; it is nulled in `closeHostileStores` so no later call can be handed a closed handle.

3. CUTOVER — the REAL mapper with two DISTINCT causes producing two DIFFERENT codes: `DurableStoreError("EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT")` -> CUTOVER_ACTIVATE_EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT, `DurableStoreError("STORE_INPUT_INVALID")` -> CUTOVER_ACTIVATE_FIELD_INVALID. The rostered arm passes a plain `Error`, which fails `instanceof DurableStoreError` on line one and lands on the STORE_UNAVAILABLE default without the mapper discriminating anything.

4. GA BINDING — grants minted through core's published `grantHumanAuthority`, never hand-written. BEFORE varies work identity ALONE (a gate minted for a foreign workRef, internally consistent, everything else valid) -> ACTIVATION_BINDING_WORK_MISMATCH. AFTER varies generation identity ALONE: a gate minted for the real work ref, one digest at 63 hex instead of 64 -> ACTIVATION_BINDING_GENERATION_UNBOUND. That second one is the strongest arm in the set, because GENERATION_UNBOUND is minted only AFTER `decideApprovalAuthority` returns ok — the code is unreachable unless the core-minted grant genuinely satisfied core, so the arm proves the human gate was passed rather than dodged.

RACE ARMS: four, each recording TWO legs, asserted PER LEG and positionally by construction order — never on an aggregate and never on which side settled first. Two of them (CUTOVER, GA BINDING) carry DIFFERENT expectations per leg, which is the whole reason `DivergenceRaceCase` exists; `HostileRaceCase`'s single `expected` would have forced both legs onto one code and erased the discrimination under test.

ONE SHARED-HELPER EDIT, disclosed rather than buried. `isAdmitted` did not recognise `status: "WITHHELD"`, so `authorizeApproval`'s refusal counted as an ADMISSION and the zero-admission assertion would have failed on a correct refusal. Added it beside the "ABSENT"/"UNKNOWN" statuses already there. It is production's OWN marker (plan-approval.ts:88), read not inferred, and it can only move a value from ADMITTED to refused — never the reverse — so the slice invariant stays exactly as strict for every other case on this axis. Measured before editing: zero occurrences of `"WITHHELD"` anywhere in tests/security, and the only producer in apps/ or packages/ is plan-approval.ts itself. The 221 pre-existing tests still pass unchanged, which is the evidence that it is inert for them.
